20: // signed and unsigned integers.

22:   template <typename T> static bool fits_in_int(T value) {
23:     unsigned max = max_value<int>();

71: template <typename T, typename Context> class arg_converter {
72:  private:
73:   using char_type = typename Context::char_type;
74: 
75:   basic_format_arg<Context>& arg_;
76:   char_type type_;
77: 
78:  public:
79:   arg_converter(basic_format_arg<Context>& arg, char_type type)
80:       : arg_(arg), type_(type) {}
81: 
82:   void operator()(bool value) {
83:     if (type_ != 's') operator()<bool>(value);
84:   }
85: 
86:   template <typename U, FMT_ENABLE_IF(std::is_integral<U>::value)>
87:   void operator()(U value) {
88:     bool is_signed = type_ == 'd' || type_ == 'i';
89:     using target_type = conditional_t<std::is_same<T, void>::value, U, T>;
90:     if (const_check(sizeof(target_type) <= sizeof(int))) {
91:       // Extra casts are used to silence warnings.
92:       if (is_signed) {
93:         arg_ = detail::make_arg<Context>(
94:             static_cast<int>(static_cast<target_type>(value)));
95:       } else {
96:         using unsigned_type = typename make_unsigned_or_bool<target_type>::type;
97:         arg_ = detail::make_arg<Context>(
98:             static_cast<unsigned>(static_cast<unsigned_type>(value)));
99:       }
100:     } else {
101:       if (is_signed) {
102:         // glibc's printf doesn't sign extend arguments of smaller types:
103:         //   std::printf("%lld", -42);  // prints "4294967254"
104:         // but we don't have to do the same because it's a UB.
105:         arg_ = detail::make_arg<Context>(static_cast<long long>(value));
106:       } else {
107:         arg_ = detail::make_arg<Context>(
108:             static_cast<typename make_unsigned_or_bool<U>::type>(value));
109:       }
110:     }
111:   }
112: 
113:   template <typename U, FMT_ENABLE_IF(!std::is_integral<U>::value)>
114:   void operator()(U) {}  // No conversion needed for non-integral types.
115: };

154:  private:

389: template <typename OutputIt, typename Char>
390: void basic_printf_context<OutputIt, Char>::parse_flags(format_specs& specs,
391:                                                        const Char*& it,
392:                                                        const Char* end) {
393:   for (; it != end; ++it) {
394:     switch (*it) {
395:     case '-':
396:       specs.align = align::left;
397:       break;
398:     case '+':
399:       specs.sign = sign::plus;
400:       break;
401:     case '0':
402:       specs.fill[0] = '0';
403:       break;
404:     case ' ':
405:       specs.sign = sign::space;
406:       break;
407:     case '#':
408:       specs.alt = true;
409:       break;
410:     default:
411:       return;
412:     }
413:   }
414: }

426: template <typename OutputIt, typename Char>
427: int basic_printf_context<OutputIt, Char>::parse_header(const Char*& it,
428:                                                        const Char* end,
429:                                                        format_specs& specs) {
430:   int arg_index = -1;
431:   char_type c = *it;
432:   if (c >= '0' && c <= '9') {
433:     // Parse an argument index (if followed by '$') or a width possibly
434:     // preceded with '0' flag(s).
435:     detail::error_handler eh;
436:     int value = parse_nonnegative_int(it, end, eh);
437:     if (it != end && *it == '$') {  // value is an argument index
438:       ++it;
439:       arg_index = value;
440:     } else {
441:       if (c == '0') specs.fill[0] = '0';
442:       if (value != 0) {
443:         // Nonzero value means that we parsed width and don't need to
444:         // parse it or flags again, so return now.
445:         specs.width = value;
446:         return arg_index;
447:       }
448:     }
449:   }
450:   parse_flags(specs, it, end);
451:   // Parse width.
452:   if (it != end) {
453:     if (*it >= '0' && *it <= '9') {
454:       detail::error_handler eh;
455:       specs.width = parse_nonnegative_int(it, end, eh);
456:     } else if (*it == '*') {
457:       ++it;
458:       specs.width = static_cast<int>(visit_format_arg(
459:           detail::printf_width_handler<char_type>(specs), get_arg()));
460:     }
461:   }
462:   return arg_index;
463: }

465: template <typename OutputIt, typename Char>
466: template <typename ArgFormatter>
467: OutputIt basic_printf_context<OutputIt, Char>::format() {
468:   auto out = this->out();
469:   const Char* start = parse_ctx_.begin();
470:   const Char* end = parse_ctx_.end();
471:   auto it = start;
472:   while (it != end) {
473:     char_type c = *it++;
474:     if (c != '%') continue;
475:     if (it != end && *it == c) {
476:       out = std::copy(start, it, out);
477:       start = ++it;
478:       continue;
479:     }
480:     out = std::copy(start, it - 1, out);
481: 
482:     format_specs specs;
483:     specs.align = align::right;
484: 
485:     // Parse argument index, flags and width.
486:     int arg_index = parse_header(it, end, specs);
487:     if (arg_index == 0) on_error("argument not found");
488: 
489:     // Parse precision.
490:     if (it != end && *it == '.') {
491:       ++it;
492:       c = it != end ? *it : 0;
493:       if ('0' <= c && c <= '9') {
494:         detail::error_handler eh;
495:         specs.precision = parse_nonnegative_int(it, end, eh);
496:       } else if (c == '*') {
497:         ++it;
498:         specs.precision = static_cast<int>(
499:             visit_format_arg(detail::printf_precision_handler(), get_arg()));
500:       } else {
501:         specs.precision = 0;
502:       }
503:     }
504: 
505:     format_arg arg = get_arg(arg_index);
506:     if (specs.precision >= 0 && arg.type() == detail::type::cstring_type) {
507:       auto str = visit_format_arg(detail::get_cstring<Char>(), arg);
508:       auto str_end = str + specs.precision;
509:       auto nul = std::find(str, str_end, Char());
510:       arg = detail::make_arg<basic_printf_context>(basic_string_view<Char>(
511:           str,
512:           detail::to_unsigned(nul != str_end ? nul - str : specs.precision)));
513:     }
514:     if (specs.alt && visit_format_arg(detail::is_zero_int(), arg))
515:       specs.alt = false;
516:     if (specs.fill[0] == '0') {
517:       if (arg.is_arithmetic())
518:         specs.align = align::numeric;
519:       else
520:         specs.fill[0] = ' ';  // Ignore '0' flag for non-numeric types.
521:     }
522: 
523:     // Parse length and convert the argument to the required type.
524:     c = it != end ? *it++ : 0;
525:     char_type t = it != end ? *it : 0;
526:     using detail::convert_arg;
527:     switch (c) {
528:     case 'h':
529:       if (t == 'h') {
530:         ++it;
531:         t = it != end ? *it : 0;
532:         convert_arg<signed char>(arg, t);
533:       } else {
534:         convert_arg<short>(arg, t);
535:       }
536:       break;
537:     case 'l':
538:       if (t == 'l') {
539:         ++it;
540:         t = it != end ? *it : 0;
541:         convert_arg<long long>(arg, t);
542:       } else {
543:         convert_arg<long>(arg, t);
544:       }
545:       break;
546:     case 'j':
547:       convert_arg<intmax_t>(arg, t);
548:       break;
549:     case 'z':
550:       convert_arg<size_t>(arg, t);
551:       break;
552:     case 't':
553:       convert_arg<std::ptrdiff_t>(arg, t);
554:       break;
555:     case 'L':
556:       // printf produces garbage when 'L' is omitted for long double, no
557:       // need to do the same.
558:       break;
559:     default:
560:       --it;
561:       convert_arg<void>(arg, c);
562:     }
563: 
564:     // Parse type.
565:     if (it == end) FMT_THROW(format_error("invalid format string"));
566:     specs.type = static_cast<char>(*it++);
567:     if (arg.is_integral()) {
568:       // Normalize type.
569:       switch (specs.type) {
570:       case 'i':
571:       case 'u':
572:         specs.type = 'd';
573:         break;
574:       case 'c':
575:         visit_format_arg(detail::char_converter<basic_printf_context>(arg),
576:                          arg);
577:         break;
578:       }
579:     }
580: 
581:     start = it;
582: 
583:     // Format argument.
584:     visit_format_arg(ArgFormatter(out, specs, *this), arg);
585:   }
586:   return std::copy(start, it, out);
587: }

part.text:
Fixed. The bug was in `printf_arg_formatter::operator()` (include/fmt/printf.h:260), which unconditionally reset `align` to `align::right` for chars, discarding the `align::left` set by the `-` flag.

Changes in include/fmt/printf.h:
- Char branch now preserves left alignment, only forcing `align::right` when `-` wasn't given (also normalizing `numeric` back to `right`).
- The `'0'` flag no longer clobbers left alignment (`%-05c` → `a    `, matching glibc, which ignores `0` when `-` is present).

Verified: `%-5c` now prints `a    ` as `std::printf` does, and the full test suite passes — 17/17 tests including all printf tests (`%-5c` case) and all prior PASS_TO_PASS cases.
